text:
Maya: Heads up — main CI is red on smoke-e2e (gpu) again, intermittent GPU OOMs across a few runs. Build 9173 and 9181 both hit it. Can someone start a bisect?

Sam: on it, can you paste the failing log lines?

Maya: sure, here's the tail: 
```
[2026-03-16T14:12:01Z] smoke-e2e: starting test suite
[2026-03-16T14:12:05Z] Allocator: trying to reserve 1.2GiB
[2026-03-16T14:12:05Z] GPU OOM: failed to allocate 1.2GiB on /dev/nvidia0
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/srv/runner/test_runner.py", line 412, in run_test
    model_infer(batch)
  File "/srv/runner/infer.py", line 127, in model_infer
    raise RuntimeError("GPU OOM")
RuntimeError: GPU OOM
```

Miguel: thanks. Does the OOM always show the same allocation size? could be a kernel/regression in batching or quant code.

Anya: @sam FYI last-green for smoke-e2e-gpu was at main@c3f9a2 (around 1976520000). Might be between that and HEAD.

sam: starting automated bisect now with `./tools/ci-bisect --range c3f9a2..HEAD --test smoke-e2e --env gpu` — will post progress.

ci-bot: bisect started by sam — range c3f9a2..main HEAD (approx 120 commits). Current probe: main~60 (commit a1b2c3).

Maya: quick note — two PRs merged yesterday touched the allocator and the attention kernel scheduling. Suspect those.

sam: probe at main~60 failed (OOM). advancing to main~30.

ryan: if bisect narrows to the allocator PR I can roll back the change for a quick test in staging.

sam: probe main~30 passed. narrowing between main~60..main~30. Next probe main~45.

ci-bot: probe main~45 failed (OOM). Suspect range main~60..main~45.

Anya: can we get a reproducible local run? I can try to reproduce with smaller batch on a dev GPU to see if it's allocation growth vs fragmentation.

sam: good idea. I'm going to add `--memprofile` and `--kv-cache-debug` to the next probe to capture alloc patterns.

Maya: also seeing a flaky test `infer_batch_randomized` that spikes memory occasionally — might be the same issue. Tagging @miguel for attention kernel changes.

miguel: pinged. I'll look at the kernel scheduling PR diff and the allocator tweak. If bisect points at my PR I'll prepare a revert.

sam: bisect finished: first bad commit identified: 2f9d7b3 — "async-batching: prefer eager kernel scheduling" by miguel.

Maya: wow ok. @miguel can you confirm locally? If you can't reproduce, we should try reverting on a staging lane.

miguel: reproducing now with stress script. so far reproduces reliably with 8-concurrent inferences. Investigating.

ryan: once confirmed let's do a revert PR and a fast rollout to Dedicated staging. I can own the revert and smoke validation.

sam: created revert PR #4567 with revert of 2f9d7b3, running CI. cc @oncall for staging deploy window.

oncall: staging window open in 10m, I can deploy the revert after CI passes.

Maya: appreciate it — please include the memprofile logs in the PR.

miguel: digging into the scheduling heuristics — looks like eager scheduling increases pinned allocations in some traces which pushes memory over the limit. I'll add a guard.

sam: CI for revert passed on smoke-e2e (gpu). deploying to staging now.

oncall: deployed revert to staging. running 10x smoke-e2e runs now.

ci-bot: staging runs: 10/10 passed.

Maya: ✅ staging looks clean. Can we merge revert to main and queue a patch release?

ryan: merging revert PR now, will trigger release pipeline.

miguel: thanks everyone — I'll open a follow-up PR with a safer scheduling fix and tests to avoid regression.

Maya: great, thanks for the quick triage. Closing thread once revert is in main. :thumbsup:
